title: TopicGPT: A Prompt-based Topic Modeling Framework

paper.version_read: NAACL 2024 long paper (ACL Anthology PDF), external/papers/W4401043789.txt
paper.repo_commit: e6499ef7f3db8bba2bcff30e4d636b11d2acc97d (HEAD 2026-05-15; repo refactored into the topicgpt_python package after publication; clone external/repos/W4401043789/chtmp223__topicGPT)

dependence.note: The LLM is the topic generator (GPT-4), refiner (GPT-4) and assigner (GPT-3.5-turbo) inside the pipeline; the reported alignment metrics are computed on its assignments.

claim.statement: TopicGPT (GPT-4 topic generation + GPT-3.5-turbo assignment) is substantially more aligned with human ground-truth labels than LDA, BERTopic and SeededLDA on Wiki and Bills: refined-topic harmonic purity P1 = 0.74 (Wiki, k=22) and 0.57 (Bills, k=24) vs LDA 0.64 / 0.52, BERTopic 0.58 / 0.39, SeededLDA 0.62 / 0.52 (Table 1).
claim.metric: Harmonic purity P1, Adjusted Rand Index, NMI between predicted topic assignments and gold labels (topicgpt_python/metrics.py calculate_metrics; only the first assigned topic retained)
claim.original_source: Paper Table 1 (Sec. 5.1); cost Table 11 (Bills 88 USD, Wiki 155 USD at 2023 prices); dataset stats Table 12

protocol.model: gpt-4 (undated alias, 8,192-token context per footnote 6 -> gpt-4-0314 or gpt-4-0613; default results finalized Aug 2023, ablations Oct 2023) for generation/refinement; gpt-3.5-turbo (4,096-token context -> 0301/0613) for assignment; Mistral-7B-Instruct ablation. gpt-4-turbo is ONLY mentioned as future work (Limitations, footnote 8) - never an experimental arm.
protocol.model_status: dead (gpt-4-0314 2024-06-13; gpt-4-0613 and gpt-3.5-turbo-0613 2024-09-13). Live arm gpt-4-turbo not an experimental arm.
protocol.endpoint: POST https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions (repo APIClient; also Azure/Vertex/vLLM in current package)
protocol.prompt_source: prompt/generation_1.txt, prompt/generation_2.txt, prompt/refinement.txt, prompt/assignment.txt, prompt/correction.txt, seed topics prompt/seed_1.md; also paper Appendix Tables 14-17
protocol.n_items: Topic generation: 1,000 (Bills) / 1,100 (Wiki) sampled docs; assignment + self-correction on test sets of 15,242 (Bills) / 8,024 (Wiki) docs (Table 12)
protocol.evaluation: Automatic: P1/ARI/NMI between first assigned topic and gold label (metrics.py); refinement = prompted merging + removal of topics <1% frequency (automatic); human annotation only in the auxiliary misalignment study (Table 3).
protocol.environment_check: Run metrics.py on the released sample outputs (data/output/sample) to validate the metric code path; verify the Google Drive datasets are still downloadable and contain gold labels.

judgment.rule: ANALYSIS_PLAN Sec. 1 on P1 (Bills refined / Wiki refined): survival = TopicGPT P1 > LDA P1 (LDA re-run locally, same k) with bootstrap CI over documents excluding 0, and the gap of the same order (original +0.10 Wiki, +0.05 Bills). Partial = direction holds but gap collapses below CI. Dead = LDA >= TopicGPT.
judgment.notes: Only judgeable on successor models; no live baseline exists.

domain_notes: Method paper where the LLM is an internal pipeline component; the headline comparison is against classical topic models that can be re-run deterministically. The scaffold's live-arm hit is an alias false positive: 'GPT-4-turbo' appears once, in the Limitations section, as a suggestion for handling long documents. Because topic generation is a sequential, order-dependent process, re-runs produce different topic inventories (k varies: 79 vs 73 vs 118 in the stability ablations), so the metric must be compared at the paper's granularity (post-refinement P1), not per topic.
